summary.text: Napoleon Bonaparte rose to prominence as a general during the French Revolution and was Emperor of the French from 18 May 1804 until his first abdication in 1814.
He led military campaigns across Europe and the Middle East, and as a statesman he made legal and administrative reforms, most notably the Napoleonic Code.
He remains controversial because of his role in wars that devastated Europe, his looting of conquered territories, and his mixed record on civil rights.

items.prompt: In 1798 Napoleon led an invasion of Egypt and Syria. What role did it play in his career?

options.label: It ended his military career after a crushing defeat
It served as a springboard for his rise to political power
It made him a soldier in the royal army of the king
It gave him the throne of an island kingdom in Italy

items.explain: The invasion of Egypt and Syria in 1798 served as a springboard for his rise to political power.

items.prompt: How did Napoleon take political control of France in November 1799?

options.label: He engineered a coup against the Directory and became First Consul
He was elected Emperor by a vote of the Estates General
He defeated the Bourbons in battle and restored the king
He bought the Directory out through a deal with Britain

items.explain: Napoleon engineered the Coup of 18 Brumaire against the Directory and became First Consul of the Republic.

items.prompt: As First Consul, what did Napoleon do to consolidate his power further?

options.label: He gave up power to a council of elected deputies
He asked the pope to name a king in his place
He crowned himself Emperor of the French
He let his brother Joseph rule as First Consul

items.explain: In December 1804 Napoleon crowned himself Emperor of the French.

items.prompt: Which describes Napoleon's reforms in France and Europe?

options.label: He expanded the free press and restored directly elected government
He returned power to religious authorities and ended public schooling
He revived feudal privileges and made nobles subject to no courts
He abolished the vestiges of feudalism and enacted equality before the law

items.explain: Napoleon abolished the vestiges of feudalism, set up public education, and enacted equality before the law, while he abolished the free press and directly elected government.

items.prompt: In 1812 Napoleon invaded Russia and briefly occupied Moscow. How did the campaign end for his army?

options.label: With a lasting peace treaty signed in Moscow
With a catastrophic retreat that winter
With a final victory at the Battle of Leipzig
With a march on to Saint Petersburg and the tsar's surrender

items.explain: After the Battle of Borodino, Napoleon briefly occupied Moscow before conducting a catastrophic retreat of his army that winter.

items.prompt: Napoleon abdicated in April 1814 and was exiled to Elba. What happened next?

options.label: He stayed on the island and died there of stomach cancer
He returned as emperor and held France until his death
He escaped, reclaimed control of France, and was beaten by a Seventh Coalition
He was pardoned by the Bourbons and ruled with them

items.explain: Napoleon escaped from Elba, marched on Paris and reclaimed control, but a Seventh Coalition defeated him at Waterloo.
